# This Week in AI: The 5 Stories That Matter (September 13, 2026)

This week, AI stories spanned from the life-saving (new antibiotic research) to the personal (restoring old family photos) to the practical (yes, you can now use Python in Excel without knowing code). Let's dive into the five most important developments for everyday people.

## AI Just Accelerated the Search for New Antibiotics — And That's a Big Deal

[![AI Just Accelerated the Search for New Antibiotics — And That's a Big Deal](/assets/images/how-ai-is-speeding-up-the-hunt-for-new-antibiotics-and-what-that-means.jpg)](https://aiworldhq.com/article/how-ai-is-speeding-up-the-hunt-for-new-antibiotics-and-what-that-means.html)

For years, finding new antibiotics has been a slow, expensive process. But researchers are now using AI tools like ChatGPT to scan millions of molecules faster than any human team could. The result? The antibiotic discovery pipeline — which had practically stalled — is moving again. This matters because antibiotic-resistant bacteria are a growing threat, and we need new drugs to stay ahead. If you've ever taken antibiotics that no longer worked, this research could eventually mean better treatment options for you or your family.

[Read the full story](https://aiworldhq.com/article/how-ai-is-speeding-up-the-hunt-for-new-antibiotics-and-what-that-means.html)

## Your Old Family Photos Can Now Be Brought Back to Life

[![Your Old Family Photos Can Now Be Brought Back to Life](/assets/images/how-ai-helps-you-reimagine-old-family-photos-and-what-to-try-first.jpg)](https://aiworldhq.com/article/how-ai-helps-you-reimagine-old-family-photos-and-what-to-try-first.html)

That faded snapshot from your parents' wedding or your childhood birthday might not be gone forever. A new wave of AI tools can restore old photos — fixing colors, repairing damage, and even animating faces to create moving images. Google and other companies have made these tools surprisingly easy to use, and you don't need any technical skill. It's a way to preserve family history that feels almost magical. If you have boxes of old photos sitting somewhere, this might be the week to dig them out.

[Read the full story](https://aiworldhq.com/article/how-ai-helps-you-reimagine-old-family-photos-and-what-to-try-first.html)

## Robotaxis Are No Longer Just a Experiment — They're Picking Up Passengers Now

[![Robotaxis Are No Longer Just a Experiment — They're Picking Up Passengers Now](/assets/images/robotaxis-explained-what-s-real-what-s-hype-and-what-s-coming-to-your-.jpg)](https://aiworldhq.com/article/robotaxis-explained-what-s-real-what-s-hype-and-what-s-coming-to-your-.html)

Driverless taxis powered by AI are already operating in several cities, and they're no longer just test vehicles. Companies like Waymo (backed by Google) are letting real passengers climb in and ride across town — with no human driver behind the wheel. Yes, there are still questions about safety, regulation, and what happens to human taxi drivers. But if you live in certain cities, you might already see these cars on the road. Whether you're curious or cautious, this technology is arriving faster than many expected.

[Read the full story](https://aiworldhq.com/article/robotaxis-explained-what-s-real-what-s-hype-and-what-s-coming-to-your-.html)

## You Can Now Use Python in Excel — Even If You've Never Written Code

[![You Can Now Use Python in Excel — Even If You've Never Written Code](/assets/images/how-to-use-python-in-excel-even-if-you-ve-never-written-code.jpg)](https://aiworldhq.com/article/how-to-use-python-in-excel-even-if-you-ve-never-written-code.html)

Microsoft has quietly rolled out one of the biggest changes to Excel in years: you can now run Python directly inside your spreadsheets, without installing anything or learning a programming language. That means you can use AI-powered data analysis, automation, and visualization without typing a single line of code. For small business owners, students, or anyone who works with numbers, this opens up tools that were previously reserved for programmers. It's a small change in the spreadsheet that could make a big difference in how you work.

[Read the full story](https://aiworldhq.com/article/how-to-use-python-in-excel-even-if-you-ve-never-written-code.html)

## AI Is Starting to Show Up in Government Services — Even If You Don't Log In

[![AI Is Starting to Show Up in Government Services — Even If You Don't Log In](/assets/images/openai-s-government-ai-push-what-it-means-for-your-daily-life.jpg)](https://aiworldhq.com/article/openai-s-government-ai-push-what-it-means-for-your-daily-life.html)

OpenAI has been striking deals to put its AI tools inside public agencies — from helping caseworkers process paperwork to answering citizen questions. This matters even if you never use ChatGPT, because it could affect how you interact with government services. Faster permit approvals, better answers to questions about benefits, and smoother processing are all possible. But there are also real questions about accuracy, privacy, and whether AI should be making decisions that affect people's lives. This is one change that could touch almost everyone, whether they realize it or not.

[Read the full story](https://aiworldhq.com/article/openai-s-government-ai-push-what-it-means-for-your-daily-life.html)

## What This Means for You

AI isn't just in your phone anymore — it's showing up in your doctor's research lab, your family's photo albums, your city's streets, your work spreadsheet, and your local government office. Some of these changes will take years to fully play out. Others, like the Excel update or photo restoration tools, you could try right now. The key this week: AI is becoming more useful in everyday ways, even when you're not looking for it.
